legacy_root.title: Fresh Windows user profile: confirm hooks actually LOAD, not merely that install reported success
legacy_root.question: Question: in a brand-new Windows user profile with no prior harness state, does clean install of the plugin result in hooks that ACTUALLY EXECUTE? The named failure class is 'plugin appears installed but hooks are unloaded' (spec:11303). The probe must observe hook side effects at runtime, not the presence of a settings key - a config file is a claim, the executed hook is the receipt.

failure_class.name: plugin appears installed but hooks are unloaded

legacy_root.answer: CONFIRMED on a USERPROFILE/HOME-redirected throwaway profile (the catalog-allowed equivalent of a brand-new Windows user profile on this Linux worktree): after a clean install, SessionStart, PreToolUse and Stop each write a beacon that only the hook script writes, AND the harness inventory lists the same three hooks. With the plugin uninstalled both signals stay silent. Injecting a top-level $schema key (the Codex deny_unknown_fields hole) unloads every hook while settings.json and a directory listing still claim the plugin is installed. A second install does not double-register. Settings.json was never used as evidence.

regression_diff.delta: second install did not grow hook inventory; $schema unload remains visible

legacy_root.residual_caveat: This sparse worktree does not ship a marketplace plugin zip or a native Codex/Claude Windows binary. The confirmation runs a contract-faithful packaged canary plus a deny_unknown_fields loader that reproduces the measured $schema→zero-hooks behaviour inside an isolated USERPROFILE. It does not observe a particular vendor client build's in-process hook host. Native-client re-run remains a reviewer action on Windows.
